# Convert Audio to OGG

- Route: `/tools/convert-audio-to-ogg`
- Kind: `tool`
- Category: `audio`
- Slug: `convert-audio-to-ogg`

## Summary

Turn MP3, M4A, WAV, OGG, FLAC and any other audio file into OGG at the bitrate you choose. (Audio tools)

## Details

OGG Vorbis is a free, patent-unencumbered lossy format that sounds better than MP3 at the same bitrate and is native in browsers, Android and game engines. Media Manipulator converts any common audio format to OGG in one upload, keeping the sample rate and channel layout unless you change them, and offers trimming, normalisation, EQ and the AI cleanup tools on the same form.
### What it does
- Converts MP3, WAV, M4A/AAC, OGG, Opus, FLAC, ALAC, AC3 and WMA to OGG.
- Lets you pick the bitrate, sample rate and channel layout.
- Trimming, volume, loudness normalisation and EQ happen in the same FFmpeg pass as the Vorbis encode.
- Clean a voice or remove background noise with AI before the Vorbis encoder runs.
### How to use it
1. Upload audio: An MP3, WAV, FLAC or other audio file for your game or site.
2. Adjust if needed: Pick the bitrate; trim or apply effects.
3. Convert: FFmpeg encodes OGG on our servers.
4. Download: Save the OGG file.
### Supported formats
- Input: mp3, wav, m4a, aac, ogg, opus, flac, alac, ac3, wma
- Output: ogg
- Lossy output; the bitrate you choose sets the size.
### Technical details
- OGG output uses FFmpeg's libvorbis encoder; 192 kbps is the default and a safe choice for music.
- Apple devices and some car stereos do not play OGG; use M4A or MP3 for those.
- Cover art in the source is recognised as an image attachment and does not trip the video-track check.
### Use cases
- Switch formats for a device: Make a OGG copy for a player that needs it.
- Prepare for editing: Make a small, compatible file for a project.
- One file at a time: Prepare sound effects for a game engine one file at a time.
- Clean up on the way: Take the hum out of a recording before it ships as an OGG asset.
### FAQ
Q: What is OGG?
A: OGG Vorbis is a free, patent-unencumbered lossy format that sounds better than MP3 at the same bitrate and is native in browsers, Android and game engines.
Q: Will converting to OGG improve the sound?
A: No. Apple devices and some car stereos do not play OGG; use M4A or MP3 for those.
Q: Can I trim the audio while converting to OGG?
A: Yes. Mark the start and end and the OGG contains only that part.
Q: Can I convert an M4A that has album art to OGG?
A: Yes. The cover is seen as an image attachment rather than a video track, so the job proceeds and produces audio-only Vorbis.
